entries.summary: 1351, die 3. augusti, Clerus dioecesis herbipolensis saecularis et religiosus necnon personae judiciorum saecularium herbipolensium et laici civitatis wirziburgensis a poenis promulgatis processibus papalibus tam in Ludovici quondam imperatoris fautores quam occasione provisionis episcopatus herbipolensis factis absolvuntur, Nr. 1

Datum Bamberg, anno domini millesimo trecentesimo quin-

Friedrich, by the grace of God and of the Holy Apostolic See bishop of Bamberg, commissary of the same see deputed by its authority for what is written below, make known by the tenor of these presents to all who receive them that the beloved in Christ: Johannes, elect and confirmed abbot of St. Burchard, Hermann of St. Stephen, Philipp of St. James, abbots of the Benedictine monasteries of Würzburg, as well as the chapters of the churches of Würzburg, the cathedral, St. John in Haug and the Neumünster, and the convents of the said monasteries and all and each of the conventual persons there; and specially these canons of the same cathedral church of Würzburg: Albert von Ebersberg, scholasticus; Wolfram Schenk von Rosseberg, treasurer; Albert von Hesseburg, archdeacon; Eberhard von Hohenberg; then Conrad, pastor of the parish in Haug at Würzburg, Wernher von Thuringia, priest, his associate; then Heinrich, pastor of the parish in Bleichach at Würzburg, Gerung von Tüngden, primissary there; and Albert, pastor of the parish at St. Burchard at Würzburg, and Gerhard von Mainz, priest, his associate; and other priests, associates, pupils, ecclesiastics and servants of the aforesaid parishes; then Heinrich of Würzburg of All Souls; Johann von Rosenfelt of St. Gotthard on the bridge; Johann of Sts. Felix and Adauctus in the court called zu Greuenegkart; and Conrad of the blessed apostles Philip and James at the dark chapel, chaplains of the chapels of Würzburg; then Johann von Saxonia, former cleric of Würzburg; Johann von Worms; and Heinrich the Saxon, and other priests not titled or beneficed, residing at Würzburg and serving altars in the aforesaid churches and chapels there; then Conrad called Linse von Münnerstadt; Heinrich called Remel; Johann von Northusen; Johann called Amelung; and other officials and scribes of the aforesaid archdeacons of Würzburg, also advocates, procurators, notaries, also public notaries, scribes and sealers, criers and sworn messengers, also officers of the ecclesiastical courts of Würzburg; also Johann called Bersich von Karlstadt, officer; Heinrich called Katzenstein, notary; Conrad called Vzzenhein, scribe of the kitchen of the episcopal court of Würzburg; the brothers Johann and Conrad called de Leone; Marquard called Kempff von Amberg; and Berthold called von Eychach, clerics of Würzburg; then the commanders and priors and other conventual brothers, clerical and lay, of the houses of Würzburg of the brothers of St. Mary of the Teutonic Order and of the hospital of St. John of Jerusalem; then the priors and guardians and each conventual brother of the houses of Würzburg of the Dominican, Franciscan, Augustinian and Carmelite orders; and all and each other ecclesiastical persons, religious as well as secular, of both sexes, exempt and non-exempt, and their colleges and convents, of whatever order, profession, rank, state or condition they may be, of the city of Würzburg and its suburbs, jointly or together and separately, — we, attentively considering that it is for good minds to fear guilt where no guilt is found, and that therefore, even if not under urgent necessity, at least as a salutary precaution this should be done at their urging — upon the humble and proper petition made in the person of Johann von Frankfurt, succentor of the church of Bamberg, their procurator having sufficient and special mandate for this — by the same procurator, on behalf of the souls of the same lords and persons who appointed him their procurator and special messenger and who are held to need this and such a benefit of absolution, to abide by the mandates of Holy Mother Church and our own, on the holy gospels of God touched bodily, an oath first solemnly sworn before us — and in the name of the procurator for those who appoint him, we absolve duly from suspensions, excommunications, interdict and other penalties and sentences pronounced by a man or by law, contained in the processes both apostolic at the instance of Lord Albert von Hohenberg, formerly appointed bishop of Würzburg by the same apostolic see and then translated to the church of Freising, and also ordinary by the authority of the same Lord Albert, then elect of Würzburg, in the episcopal affair of the church of Würzburg itself on behalf of the same Lord Albert von Hohenberg, then elect of Würzburg, against our venerable brother Lord Albert von Hohenloch, then not yet but now recently by divine and the same apostolic see's providence appointed bishop of Würzburg, and against those favouring and adhering to him, then issued and also promulgated, by apostolic authority committed to us in this matter, enjoining on them a salutary penance according to the measure of guilt, in the name of God in the form of the Church — the tenor of the apostolic commission made to us about it being observed in all respects — and we promulgate this absolution by these presents, and we also relax and remit in this writing the interdicts to which the church, city, towns, castles, villages and other places and lands of them and of the diocese of Würzburg are subject, and any other spiritual and temporal penalties.
Moreover, with the clerics themselves concerning the irregularity which they incurred — not however in contempt of the keys of the Church — by celebrating divine offices or involving themselves with them or ministering in the orders received, we have duly dispensed and have qualified them, and so, by dispensing and qualifying by the apostolic authority also committed to us in this, we restore them to their former state by these presents.
Also, after previous absolution of the faithful, both ecclesiastical and secular persons of both sexes, deceased there, especially those who died as Catholic Christians during the processes or at the time of the processes mentioned, we order by the same authority also committed to us for this that their bodies be handed over to ecclesiastical burial, and we permit those already buried to rest in the Lord and their souls to be helped by the suffrages of the faithful, committing and ordering likewise by the apostolic authority by which as above all prelates and pastors of churches who are requested about it to publish and have published the foregoing in the pulpits of their churches and elsewhere where it is opportune.
In testimony of which we have had the present letter fortified by the appending of our seal.
Given at Bamberg, in the year of the Lord one thousand three hundred and fifty-one, on the fourth day of the week after the feast of blessed Peter in Chains.

facts.content: absolved the clergy of the diocese of Würzburg from the penalties of the papal processes concerning supporters of Emperor Ludwig and the dispute over the see of Würzburg, as papal commissary.
